title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 4
statement: Rose fills each of the rectangular regions of her rectangular flower bed with a different type of flower. The lengths, in feet, of the rectangular regions in her flower bed are as shown in the figure. She plants one flower per square foot in each region. Asters cost \(\$1\) each, begonias \(\$1.50\) each, cannas \(\$2\) each, dahlias \(\$2.50\) each, and Easter lilies \(\$3\) each. What is the least possible cost, in dollars, for her garden?

solutions.text:
The five regions have areas \(4,\) \(6,\) \(15,\) \(20,\) and \(21\) square feet.

Cost is minimized by placing the most expensive flower in the smallest region, so the total is \[ \begin{gathered} (3)(4)+(2.5)(6)+(2)(15) \\ {}+(1.5)(20)+(1)(21) \\ = 108. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Find the area of each of the five regions first
To minimize cost, plant the most expensive flower in the smallest region
